shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab / monolith with rounded or squared top
low-relief carving on a weathered stone surface
horizontal registers or bands dividing the composition
a row of repeated motifs across the upper zone
creature heads seen in profile with prominent eye and snout/beak
raised border or frame along an edge
outdoor in-situ photograph with stone rubble/architecture behind
justification: Both are tall relief-carved stone slabs organised into horizontal registers, with a row of repeated, similarly sized motifs occupying the top zone above larger elements below, and both use shallow rounded relief on eroded stone. The difference is fundamental: A is a rigid, fully packed grid of equal-sized curvilinear cartouche-like blocks confined within a raised frame, while B is a sparse, asymmetrical field of recognisable animals and a chevron band with large blank ground between them.
